name: Modulation basics: LFO vs envelope, then mod-matrix source→destination routing
goal: Use LFOs for cyclic motion (tremolo, vibrato, wobble, WT/PWM drift; audio-rate into AM/FM) and ADSR envelopes for note-triggered shapes (amp dynamics, filter envelope ±amount for pluck/wah), then route any source (LFO, envelope, mod wheel, key, pedal) through a modulation matrix to one or more destinations (pitch, cutoff, amp, pan, delay time/feedback/amount) with set amounts—auditing hard-to-hear routes on pitch first.

sources.title: Sound Design Theory: LFO & Envelope explained!
Using Modulation Matrix for Advanced Sounds – Synth Clips 35 – Daniel Fisher

prerequisites: Synth or Web Audio graph with at least one LFO, one ADSR, amp and filter cutoff destinations, and a modulation matrix or equivalent source→destination slots

inputs.name: motion_type
inputs.description: cyclic (LFO) vs note-shaped (envelope) vs performer control (wheel/key/pedal)

inputs.name: destination
inputs.description: amp, pitch, cutoff, PWM, wavetable position, pan, delay-*, FX param

outputs.name: mod_routes
outputs.description: Documented LFO/envelope/controller source→destination routes with amounts

constraints: Ground every step in the source YouTube-provided Show-transcript text; do not invent UI paths or numeric settings not stated there.

Original synthesis / signal-flow only — map brand UI (Ableton/Vital/Serum/VAST/etc.) to portable osc/filter/env/LFO/FX modules for Traveler-inspired or Web Audio hybrid; never rip presets, wavetables, or samples.
Prefer transferable parameter relationships over vendor-specific preset or bank names.
Not affiliated with plugin/synth vendors named in the source videos; recreate with comparable modules.
LFOs and envelopes are control modules—they make no sound alone; movement is the design goal.
Velocity→filter expression is a separate, more specific skill: velocity-filter-cutoff-envelope-amount.

steps.action: Treat LFO as a very slow oscillator (usually below hearing): set shape (sine/tri/square/saw/custom) and rate, then assign to a destination so the parameter follows the oscillation.

Classic LFO recipes: → amp = tremolo; → pitch = vibrato; → low-pass cutoff = wobble; → waveform/PWM/WT position = evolving source timbre. Tempo-sync for rhythmic motion or keep slow free-rate for subtle drift.
steps.expect: Audible cyclic change on chosen param

steps.action: Raise LFO rate into audio range: amp mod → AM sidebands; pitch mod → FM-like spectra; very fast FX-param mod (e.g. phaser) can become a distortion/timbre effect.
If available, try LFO one-shot mode—shape plays once, behaving like an envelope.

Amp envelope ADSR: Attack = fade-in time; Decay = time to sustain; Sustain = held level (if sustain = max, decay has no effect); Release = fade-out after key-up. Percussive: attack+sustain low, length from decay (+ some release). Pad/violin-like: longer attack+release, sustain full.

Filter envelope: assign to cutoff with ±amount/depth. Positive amount opens from a low cutoff (plucky bass with short A, some D, no S, short R). Negative amount with high cutoff can wah downward; longer attack + positive amount opens wah; raise sustain to keep open while held.
Ensure amp envelope lets enough signal through to hear filter motion. Also try envelopes on PWM or wavetable position so the source evolves per note.

Mod matrix: Treat the mod matrix as deep synthesis: any controller source (self-running LFO/env or performer control like wheel/key/pedal) can move any available audible destination (pitch, cutoff, amp, vibrato rate, pan, delay params, …).
steps.expect: Source and destination lists identified on the instrument

steps.action: On an init/simple patch, create a route: choose source, choose destination, raise amount. Prefer starting with destination = oscillator pitch so the modulation shape is immediately audible.
steps.expect: Clear audible modulation when source moves

steps.action: Example performer control: mod wheel → filter cutoff. Lower cutoff, raise amount, move wheel; set wheel to max while trimming amount for the brightest intended ceiling. Add resonance/delay for musicality.
steps.expect: Wheel opens filter to a defined max

steps.action: Retarget or add destinations: pan, volume, delay amount/regen/time, etc. Stack multiple routes so several parameters move together for evolving pads.
If a route is hard to hear on its real destination, temporarily assign that source to pitch to audit the shape, then reconnect to the intended destination with an appropriate amount.
steps.expect: Modulation shape understood before final routing

verification: LFO motion repeats without new notes; envelope retriggers per note
Amp + filter envelopes cooperate (filter decay audible under amp)
At least one explicit source→destination→amount route exists
Modulation is audible (pitch audit used if needed)
Mod wheel or LFO/env successfully drives a non-default destination (e.g. filter or delay)
